speaker.name: Kelbin
colour_lines: Muleteers sing as they cross so the ones ahead will hear them in the cloud.
The Windward Waystation keeps odd hours, so knock twice, wait, and do not take it personally.
A shopkeeper swears the guard was in town three nights running.
own_lines: I was brought up in a mill town where everyone knew everyone's business.
I carried letters for a grain merchant. I know most of the lanes between the towns around here.
I walked alone to the nearest great city at fifteen. It took eleven days and one very lucky ride on a hay cart.
I do the small job as well as the great one. Nobody can tell the difference until it matters.
I have a neighbour I have been competing with for thirty years. I would be lost without them.
I want this errand finished and a whole day of sleep after. In that order, if luck allows.
Muleteers sing as they cross so the ones ahead will hear them in the cloud.
The Windward Waystation keeps odd hours, so knock twice, wait, and do not take it personally.
A shopkeeper swears the guard was in town three nights running.
Tomas is a watch sergeant at the Windward Waystation.
I swore to an old friend that the iron coffer would reach Tomas.
Tonight I may not keep my word.
My friend is gone now.
This is all I have left of the promise, and I won't see it lost.
Thank you.
Tomas will be at the Windward Waystation.
Get me there, and my promise is kept.
Thank you.
We can catch our breath here.
I carried the iron coffer once before, as a child, walking beside my grandmother. I was too small to know what it meant.

exchanges.hero_words: What is the trouble, Kelbin? Why did you send for us?
exchanges.reply: I take the small duty as seriously as the great one; no one sees the difference until it matters. I swore the iron coffer would reach Tomas, and I fear I may fail that promise tonight. Will you help me see it delivered?

new_material.line: I do the small job as well as the great one. Nobody can tell the difference until it matters.
I have a neighbour I have been competing with for thirty years. I would be lost without them.

exchanges.hero_words: Tell me about Tomas Whitlock. Can we trust them?
exchanges.reply: To be exact, I cannot vouch for Tomas. I have no measure of their trustworthiness.

exchanges.hero_words: Who or what might stand in our way on the road to Windward Waystation?
exchanges.reply: To be exact, I cannot say who might stand in your way. Muleteers sing as they cross, so those ahead can hear them in the cloud. At the Windward Waystation, knock twice and wait; they keep odd hours.

exchanges.hero_words: How long do we have, and what should we watch for?
exchanges.reply: To be exact. I do the small job as well as the great one. Nobody can tell the difference until it matters. Watch the road, and ask me what I know of the trouble on it.

new_material.line: I carried the iron coffer once before, as a child, walking beside my grandmother. I was too small to know what it meant.

exchanges.hero_words: Anything else before we set out?
exchanges.reply: To be exact, I carried letters for a grain merchant and know most of the lanes between the towns around here. That may serve us better than more talk. Come, Brakka; let us set out.
